label: D1 detector: unrewarded S1 two trials back, then reached S2 (strongest after a1 S1 u)
terms: (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (prev_state == 2) * (tv("action", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (prev_state == 2) * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -3) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (prev_state == 2) * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * prev_reward ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 1)
explanation: Sparse feature (nonzero on 1.8% of steps), active only at D1. Its magnitude is driven by a two-trial history: the trial before last reached S1 and was unrewarded, and the last trial reached S2. A small base effect (fitted weight ~0.17) gets much larger when that earlier S1 trial was an a1 choice, i.e. common unrewarded (+1.13). It is larger again if the trial three back was also unrewarded (+1.0), if the last S2 trial was rewarded (+0.41), and if the last choice was a1 (a1 S2 rare, +0.23). The last trial alone explains little (table 0.05), and choice/state, future reward, hidden good state and since_rev add nothing. Some large activations at the window start (rel=-3) cannot be predicted because their history falls outside the window. Five terms, all using observed past variables only: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.476, test 0.469, above the additive all ceiling of 0.33.

issues: The core claim holds. A single term, D1 * (a1 S1 u two trials back) * (prev_state == S2), reaches test R^2 0.434 on its own, against 0.469 for all five terms. The 'only at D1' claim is also correct: the timing baseline and every residual at GO and D2 are 0.

The claim that a last choice of a1 (a1 S2 rare) adds +0.23 is not supported. With the two-back trial fixed at a1 S1 u, the per-cell weights are: prev unrewarded 1.78 after a1 vs 1.61 after a2; prev rewarded 2.10 after a1 vs 2.20 after a2. Dropping the prev_action term changes test R^2 from 0.4686 to 0.4683.

'Grows further if the trial three back was also unrewarded (+1.0)' is attributed to the wrong variable. Split by state, the -3 unrewarded effect is +1.37 when that trial was S1 and +0.50 when it was S2. When an 'a1 S1 u at -3' term is added, the generic 'reward -3 == 0' weight drops from 1.0 to 0.24. The real driver is repeated S1-unrewarded evidence.

The explanation misses a whole history class. a1 S1 u at -3, then a2 S1 u (rare) at -2, then S2 gets a fitted weight of 2.49 (test R^2 rises from 0.469 to 0.487). The claimed terms predict about 0.2 for these windows. For example, in the worst-fit window t74 a1 S1 u, t75 a2 S1R u, t76 S2 r, the core trial t77 is actual 4.03 vs predicted 0.24. The basic 'a2 S1 u two back' pattern alone is weak (weight 0.13 to 0.17).

What is left is mostly windows whose history lies outside the window (rel -3/-2 firing of about 3.9 predicted at about 0.07) plus a small under-prediction at D1 after a1 S2 r (+0.03 to +0.07). There is no large systematic phase error. The value decile 8 residual (+1.54) adds nothing beyond the history terms (0.4866 vs 0.4863).
